Requirement R14 (input): Input Sensor Move. Fixed modalities: Wearable/HMD and Touch. Intent: Allow the pilot to move/aim the UAV's sensor..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-14.1, F-14.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-14.<F>.1, Be-14.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-14.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** R14 lets the pilot move/aim the UAV's ISR sensor toward a target/point/area, using Wearable/HMD and Touch modalities. This maps to UC 6.2 (Move Sensor to POI/AOI).

**Function candidates:**

**F-14.1 — Command sensor line-of-sight to a designated point/area.**
Goal: the pilot designates a discrete geographic/target location and the sensor is directed there. Endpoint-driven ("aim at THAT"). The pilot picks a destination; the system computes the slew.

**F-14.2 — Continuously steer/slew the sensor aim in real time.**
Goal: the pilot directly drives sensor pointing as an ongoing control (rate/direction steering), not a one-shot destination. Closed-loop manual aiming, useful for tracking a moving or not-yet-fixed target while watching the feed.

**F-14.3 — Redirect sensor aim by referencing the live feed itself.**
Goal: the pilot re-aims by acting on the displayed sensor imagery (designate a feature within the current view to re-center on), rather than on a map or via free steering. Feed-relative recentering.

These are genuinely distinct goals: F-14.1 is *destination designation* (where the target already has a known position), F-14.2 is *manual continuous steering* (no fixed destination, live control), F-14.3 is *image-relative recentering* (operate on what you see, not on a map).

Note F-14.1 overlaps conceptually with R05/R07's map-anchored designation pattern — if we go that route, structure reuse is likely. Flagging now; will confirm at structure layer.

Which function do you want to carry forward?

You're right to push. F-14.3 as I wrote it ("designate a feature within the current view to re-center") describes *how* the pilot acts — that's interaction flow, i.e. Behaviour, not teleology.

The underlying *goal* it was gesturing at is still distinct, though: aiming the sensor relative to what's currently observed vs. relative to an external map/coordinate. If I strip the mechanism, the function is just "aim the sensor at a target" — which collapses into F-14.1.

So drop F-14.3. It's not a separate function; "acting on the live feed" is a Behaviour option under F-14.1 (feed-relative designation) or under F-14.2 (steering while watching feed).

Revised function set:

**F-14.1 — Command sensor line-of-sight to a designated target/point/area** (endpoint designation; system slews to it).

**F-14.2 — Continuously steer the sensor aim in real time** (manual closed-loop pointing; no fixed destination).

These two are the genuine distinct goals. Which do you carry forward?

Both carried forward: **F-14.1** (designate endpoint) and **F-14.2** (continuous steering). They're complementary — designation for known targets, steering for live/manual aiming.

Moving to **Behaviour**. Fixed modalities for R14: **Wearable/HMD** and **Touch**. One pathway per modality, plus Mixed if it adds value. Redundancy rule applies: pilot must complete each function via either modality alone.

---

**F-14.1 — Command sensor to designated point/area**

**Be-14.1.1 (Touch-only):** Pilot taps a location on Map view (or on the live feed frame) → the tapped point becomes the sensor aimpoint → commit sends the slew command. Reuses the R05/R07 map-anchored designate-then-commit pattern.

**Be-14.1.2 (HMD-only):** Pilot looks at the target (head/eye gaze on HMD), dwell or gaze-cue designates the aimpoint → commit (blink/dwell-hold) sends slew. Hands-free — valuable when hands are on HOTAS.

**Be-14.1.3 (Mixed):** Gaze coarse-designates the region, Touch refines the exact point, then commit. Adds value: gaze is fast but imprecise; touch tightens it. Worth keeping for a designation task where precision matters.

---

**F-14.2 — Continuously steer sensor aim in real time**

**Be-14.2.1 (Touch-only):** Drag gesture on the feed/map — sensor slews in rate proportional to drag direction/magnitude; release stops. Direct-manipulation steering.

**Be-14.2.2 (HMD-only):** Head-slaved steering — sensor aim follows head pointing continuously while an engage condition is held; look-to-slew. Hands-free continuous control.

**Be-14.2.3 (Mixed):** Head slews coarse, Touch drag trims fine. Possible but for continuous steering the handoff between the two mid-slew is awkward — I'd lean toward *dropping* the mixed here unless you see value; the two standalone paths already cover it redundantly.

---

Recommendation: keep all three under F-14.1 (mixed genuinely adds precision), keep only the two standalone under F-14.2. Agree, or want the F-14.2 mixed retained?

.1
The Touch only option could be a press and hold and them select the option on the ring
The HMD could be confirmed by a button pressed on HOTAS or in the keyboard (which I forgot the name)

.2
.1 doesnt make sense
.2 similar to the .2, but with conitnuos movement of the head

Adjustments noted. Reworking both.

---

**F-14.1 — Command sensor to designated point/area**

**Be-14.1.1 (Touch-only):** Press-and-hold on Map/feed location → option ring appears → select "Move Sensor Here" (or POI/AOI variant) → commits slew. Reuses R05/R07 press-hold→option-ring pattern directly.

**Be-14.1.2 (HMD-only):** Gaze/head designates the aimpoint on the visor → confirm via HOTAS button or **UCP** keyboard press → commits slew. (UCP = the Up Front Control Panel you were reaching for; it's a Keyboard-class surface.)

*Note:* strictly, HOTAS/UCP confirm makes this HMD+Keyboard, not HMD-only. Since R14's fixed modalities are HMD and Touch, the pure-HMD confirm would be gaze-dwell/blink. Do you want the confirm to be gaze-dwell (keeps it HMD-only and modality-compliant), or are you deliberately bringing Keyboard in as the commit trigger? If the latter, this becomes a Mixed pathway rather than HMD-only.

**Be-14.1.3 (Mixed):** Gaze coarse-designates region → Touch refines exact point → commit. Kept.

---

**F-14.2 — Continuously steer sensor aim in real time**

Dropped **Be-14.2.1** (touch-drag) per your call.

**Be-14.2.2 (HMD-only):** Head-slaved continuous steering — sensor aim follows head pointing while an engage condition is held; look-to-slew, release to stop. This is the primary path.

You said ".2 similar to the .2, but with continuous movement of the head" — that *is* Be-14.2.2. So F-14.2 resolves to a single HMD continuous head-slew behaviour. No Touch path survives here, which means F-14.2 is **not modality-redundant** — only HMD can do continuous steering.

That's a conflict with the redundancy rule. Two options:
- **(a)** Accept F-14.2 as HMD-exclusive (continuous steering is inherently a head/gaze capability; Touch-drag was rejected and no other Touch form fits).
- **(b)** Reinstate a Touch continuous form (drag-to-slew) to satisfy redundancy, even if less natural.

Which? And confirm the Be-14.1.2 commit question above.

I think that the F-14.2 should be consider a behaviour of the F-14.1
So at the end would be somethin like
Be-14.1.1 (Touch-only): Press-and-hold on Map/feed location → option ring appears → select "Move Sensor Here" (or POI/AOI variant) → commits slew. Reuses R05/R07 press-hold→option-ring pattern directly.
Be-14.1.2 (HMD-only): Gaze/head designates the aimpoint on the visor → confirm via HOTAS button or UCP keyboard press → commits slew. (UCP = the Up Front Control Panel you were reaching for; it's a Keyboard-class surface.)
Be-14.1.3 (HMD-only): Head-slaved continuous steering — sensor aim follows head pointing while an engage condition is held; look-to-slew, release to stop. This is the primary path.
And the F-14.2 would be removed

Agreed — collapse to F-14.1 only. Continuous steering becomes an alternative *behaviour* for achieving the same goal (get the sensor aimed where the pilot wants), not a separate function. F-14.2 removed.

Final Behaviour set under **F-14.1 — Command sensor line-of-sight to a designated target/point/area:**

**Be-14.1.1 (Touch-only):** Press-and-hold on Map/feed location → option ring → select "Move Sensor Here" (POI/AOI variant) → commits slew. Reuses R05/R07 press-hold→option-ring pattern.

**Be-14.1.2 (HMD-only):** Gaze/head designates aimpoint on visor → confirm via HOTAS button or UCP press → commits slew.

**Be-14.1.3 (HMD-only):** Head-slaved continuous steering — aim follows head pointing while engage condition held; look-to-slew, release to stop.

Two flags before Structure:

1. **Be-14.1.2 commit** still uses HOTAS/UCP (Keyboard-class), so it's not strictly HMD-only. Given both HMD behaviours (.2 and .3) need a hands-free engage/confirm, cleanest is a **HOTAS-resident engage button** shared across both — but that pulls a non-R14 modality in as the trigger. Do you accept HOTAS/UCP as the commit for the HMD paths (pragmatic, hands-on-throttle), or want a pure gaze-dwell commit to keep HMD paths modality-pure?

2. Redundancy holds at the **function** level now: Touch (.1) and HMD (.2/.3) both fully achieve F-14.1. Good.

Resolve flag 1, then I'll propose Structures.

1. yes
2. Maybe a conitnuos movemente should also be added to the Touchscreen using a Swipe our the Touchpad

Both resolved.

1. HOTAS/UCP accepted as commit for HMD paths.
2. Adding a Touch continuous-steer path — restores modality redundancy for the *continuous* behaviour too (not just designation).

**TDC (touchpad)** is the natural fit here: it's the confirmed HOTAS-resident relative/rate cursor device — rate-based steering without taking the hand off throttle. WAD swipe also works (absolute-surface drag → rate slew) but requires a hand on the display. I'd offer both, TDC as primary since it's hands-on-throttle like the HMD head-slew.

Final Behaviour set under **F-14.1:**

**Be-14.1.1 (Touch-only, discrete):** Press-and-hold on Map/feed → option ring → "Move Sensor Here" → commit slew. (Reuses R05/R07.)

**Be-14.1.2 (HMD-only, discrete):** Gaze/head designates aimpoint → confirm via HOTAS/UCP → commit slew.

**Be-14.1.3 (HMD-only, continuous):** Head-slaved steering — aim follows head while engage held; release stops.

**Be-14.1.4 (Touch-only, continuous):** Rate-slew via TDC deflection (primary) or WAD swipe-drag on feed — sensor slews proportional to input; release/center stops. Touch-side counterpart to Be-14.1.3.

Redundancy now clean at both the discrete level (.1 Touch / .2 HMD) and continuous level (.3 HMD / .4 Touch).

Confirm this set, then I move to Structure.

Behaviour layer closed. Moving to **Structure** for F-14.1 across Be-14.1.1–.4.

Structure candidates (concrete HMI elements on fixed surfaces):

---

**S-14.1.*.1 — Map-anchored designation set (serves Be-14.1.1)**
- **Map view + live-feed frame** (WAD): tappable surfaces for press-and-hold.
- **Option ring** (WAD overlay): reused from R05/R07, with a "Move Sensor Here / POI / AOI" segment added.
- **Sensor-aimpoint glyph layer** (WAD overlay): marks the commanded aimpoint + current sensor footprint.
- **Ack** via shared R08 notification stack (slew-complete confirmation).
- *Shared:* option ring, marker/glyph layer, R08 ack — all reused across R05/R07/R14.

---

**S-14.1.*.2 — HMD designate-and-slew set (serves Be-14.1.2 + Be-14.1.3)**
- **HMD visor reticle** (in-visor output): shows gaze/head aimpoint over forward view + feed footprint.
- **Head/eye-tracking** (HMD input): drives designation (.2) and continuous head-slew (.3).
- **HOTAS engage/confirm button** (accepted extension) or **UCP key** (Keyboard): commits discrete designation (.2) and holds engage for continuous steer (.3).
- **Sensor-aimpoint glyph** mirrored on WAD + HUD strip for cross-check.
- *Shared:* aimpoint glyph layer (with S-14.1.*.1); HUD strip reused from R13.

---

**S-14.1.*.3 — Continuous rate-slew set (serves Be-14.1.4)**
- **TDC** (confirmed extension): rate-based cursor/aim deflection, hands-on-throttle.
- **WAD swipe zone** on the feed frame (Touch): drag → rate slew, as the WAD-resident alternative.
- **Rate/direction indicator** (WAD overlay): shows current slew vector + footprint moving live.
- **Sensor-aimpoint glyph layer** shared with the above sets.
- *Shared:* glyph layer; TDC also usable as the cursor for placing the .1 press-hold point if desired.

---

Note the glyph/footprint layer and R08 ack recur across all three sets — genuinely shared, not duplicated. Each set is distinct: S1 map-designation, S2 HMD gaze/head, S3 rate-steering surfaces.

Want all three (they map cleanly one-per-behaviour-group), or consolidate?

All three structures confirmed.

**R14 — closed. Final summary:**

**Function**
- **F-14.1** — Command sensor line-of-sight to a designated target/point/area. (F-14.2 continuous-steering collapsed into F-14.1 as behaviours; feed-relative F-14.3 dropped as behaviour-level.)

**Behaviour** (all under F-14.1, modality-redundant at discrete and continuous levels)
- **Be-14.1.1** (Touch, discrete): press-and-hold → option ring → "Move Sensor Here" → commit.
- **Be-14.1.2** (HMD, discrete): gaze/head designate → HOTAS/UCP confirm → commit.
- **Be-14.1.3** (HMD, continuous): head-slaved steering, engage-held, release stops.
- **Be-14.1.4** (Touch, continuous): TDC rate-slew (primary) / WAD swipe-drag alternative.

**Structure**
- **S-14.1.*.1** — Map-anchored designation set (Map/feed + option ring + aimpoint glyph + R08 ack). Serves Be-14.1.1. *Shares option ring, glyph layer, R08 ack with R05/R07/R08.*
- **S-14.1.*.2** — HMD designate-and-slew set (visor reticle + head/eye-tracking + HOTAS/UCP commit + WAD/HUD glyph mirror). Serves Be-14.1.2 + .3. *Shares glyph layer; HUD strip reused from R13.*
- **S-14.1.*.3** — Continuous rate-slew set (TDC + WAD swipe zone + rate/direction indicator + shared glyph). Serves Be-14.1.4.

Shared-element flags logged for later consolidation: option ring, aimpoint/footprint glyph layer, R08 notification stack, R13 HUD strip.

R14 complete.
